title: Strong Subadditivity: The Deepest Classical Information Inequality
content: **Strong subadditivity (SSA)** of Shannon entropy: for any joint distribution $p(x,y,z)$, $H(X,Y,Z) + H(Y) \leq H(X,Y) + H(Y,Z)$. Equivalently: (1) conditional mutual information is nonnegative, $I(X;Z|Y) \geq 0$; (2) more conditioning reduces entropy, $H(X|Y,Z) \leq H(X|Y)$. **Proof strategy** (carried out in the parent `Proofs/ShannonEntropy.lean`): the deficit $H(X,Y)+H(Y,Z)-H(X,Y,Z)-H(Y) = I(X;Z|Y)$ is written as a block sum of KL-divergence terms $p\log(p/q) \geq p - q$ (Gibbs), which telescopes to $1 - 1 = 0$, so the deficit is $\geq 0$. This file is the slim gallery entry: it re-exports the verified theorem and adds two three-variable corollaries not present in the parent (3 theorems, 0 definitions, 0 axioms, 0 sorries).
mathContext: SSA was **conjectured** by Lanford and Robinson in 1968 and **proved** by Lieb and Ruskai in 1973, first for the quantum (von Neumann entropy) case using the deep Lieb concavity theorem. The classical Shannon case is simpler — it follows from the Gibbs inequality $D(p \| q) \geq 0$. SSA implies ordinary subadditivity ($H(X,Y) \leq H(X)+H(Y)$) and is strictly stronger. In quantum information theory SSA is fundamental for quantum error correction, channel capacities, and the monogamy of entanglement.

title: strong_subadditivity: The Headline Theorem (Re-Exported, 0 Sorries)
content: **strong_subadditivity**: $H(X,Y,Z) + H(Y) \leq H(X,Y) + H(Y,Z)$, stated for `shannonEntropy` of `pXYZ` and its marginals `marginalXY`, `marginalYZ`, `marginalY`. The proof is a one-liner, `InformationTheory.strong_subadditivity hp hsum`, delegating to the fully machine-checked theorem in `Proofs/ShannonEntropy.lean`. Contrary to an earlier draft that carried a `sorry` for the KL step, this entry is **verified with 0 sorries and 0 axioms** — the KL / conditional-MI argument is discharged in the parent.
mathContext: The hypotheses `hp : ∀ xyz, 0 ≤ pXYZ xyz` and `hsum : ∑ xyz, pXYZ xyz = 1` say $p$ is a genuine probability distribution. The parent proof expresses the deficit as $I(X;Z|Y) = \sum_y p_Y(y)\, D\big(p(x,z\mid y) \,\|\, p(x\mid y)p(z\mid y)\big)$ and bounds each block by the Gibbs inequality $p\log(p/q) \geq p - q$; the blocks telescope to $1 - 1 = 0$, giving $I(X;Z|Y) \geq 0$, which is exactly SSA.

title: conditioning_reduces_entropy_general: H(X | Y,Z) ≤ H(X | Y)
content: **conditioning_reduces_entropy_general**: the three-variable form $H(X\mid Y,Z) \leq H(X\mid Y)$, written as $H(X,Y,Z) - H(Y,Z) \leq H(X,Y) - H(Y)$. It is an immediate rearrangement of strong subadditivity — subtract $H(Y,Z)$ from both sides of $H(X,Y,Z)+H(Y) \leq H(X,Y)+H(Y,Z)$ — and is closed by `linarith [InformationTheory.strong_subadditivity hp hsum]`. The deficit between the two sides is exactly the conditional mutual information $I(X;Z\mid Y) \geq 0$.
mathContext: Operationally: additional side information $Z$ can only *reduce* the remaining uncertainty about $X$ once $Y$ is known. This is the entropy-inequality face of the data-processing intuition; equality holds iff $X$ and $Z$ are conditionally independent given $Y$. The Lean proof needs no fresh computation — `linarith` derives the linear consequence directly from the SSA hypothesis.
prerequisites: definition of conditional entropy as a difference

title: conditional_mi_nonneg: I(X ; Z | Y) ≥ 0
content: **conditional_mi_nonneg**: the conditional mutual information is non-negative, $I(X;Z\mid Y) = H(X,Y) + H(Y,Z) - H(X,Y,Z) - H(Y) \geq 0$. This is the information-theoretic reading of strong subadditivity: given $Y$, the variables $X$ and $Z$ share a non-negative amount of information. Like the previous corollary it is a pure linear rearrangement, closed by `linarith [InformationTheory.strong_subadditivity hp hsum]`.
mathContext: $I(X;Z\mid Y) = \sum_y p_Y(y)\, I(X;Z \mid Y=y)$ is a $p_Y$-weighted average of ordinary (non-negative) mutual informations, so its non-negativity is equivalent to SSA. It underlies the quantum *monogamy of entanglement* and, together with `conditioning_reduces_entropy_general`, shows that the single inequality `strong_subadditivity` implies both the operational ($H(X|Y,Z) \leq H(X|Y)$) and information-theoretic ($I(X;Z|Y) \geq 0$) forms.
prerequisites: mutual information as an entropy combination
